interactive field guide

Lessons on running code you do not trust.

Twelve compact trainers, each one page, with no build step and no network calls. They cover what the walls are and how the daemon proves them, how to call it from Go or from an agent, and how the broker lets sandboxed code reach an API without ever holding the key. Four go deeper: the broker's transports, a caller's own private API, the metadata-only efficiency advisor, and the capacity signal that lets the broker back off from an overloaded API.

see one real run · physics oracle

An agent wrote a controller. A compiled cart-pole judged it.

Not a lesson: every number on that page came from one run through the docker tier on 2026-09-18. The controller was the only file the caller sent, the plant and the judge were baked into the sandbox image, and the judge recorded every 10 ms tick after running the controller as a separate process. The accepted controller balanced for 20 s and produced the same trajectory fingerprint twice; the agent's first draft dropped the pole at 5.96 s. Replay both in the browser.
